old_caption: The video captures a serene sunset scene over a calm body of water, likely a river or lake. The sun is positioned low on the horizon, casting a warm golden glow across the sky and reflecting off the water's surface. The sky transitions from a deep blue at the top to a gradient of orange and pink near the horizon. Silhouettes of trees and palm trees line the far shore, adding depth to the landscape. caption: The video captures a view across a calm river, the sun hanging low and right of center against a warm horizon. The sky grades from deep blue overhead to warm orange near the horizon, with a thin wispy cloud at upper left. A dark, leafy tree silhouettes the left edge, while the far bank carries palms, light poles and small structures. A bright vertical column of sun-glitter reflects on the water directly below the sun. This shimmering streak changes length and shape as surface ripples modulate it, sometimes unbroken, sometimes broken. The framing remains broadly steady, holding tree, horizon and sun in near-constant positions. Near the latter part, a small dark speck, consistent with a bird, appears left of the tall pole and drifts rightward. It keeps moving until it enters the glow just left of the sun, animating the otherwise calm scene with the lone bird.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
